interpretation.summary: The visible projections contain no explicit current-versus-prior management guidance comparison. The only forward-looking management language is a general outlook heading and a customer-payment expectation, neither of which establishes a material upward change in guidance level, timing, or conviction versus prior guidance. No qualifying guidance acceleration is evidenced.

Disclosures show material dependence on specific customers: a significant regional airline customer with delayed collections, past-due receivables, and a terminated PBH program, plus a U.S. Government customer whose Next Generation Pallet program was terminated for convenience. These indicate concentration risk with limited replication evidence, supporting a negative assessment.

Completed financing actions materially increased leverage and dilution risk: AAR issued $550.0 million of 6.75% Senior Notes due 2029 and borrowed $186.2 million under the Amended Revolving Credit Facility to fund the Product Support acquisition, lifting long-term debt to $986.7 million as of November 30, 2024. The company also executed a Share Purchase Agreement to exit its Indian joint venture, releasing a $9.4 million debt guarantee. These are completed, binding actions that expand debt obligations and interest burden, a negative point-in-time effect on runway and dilution/distress profile.
